frag_micro_component_size → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Fish in larger contact components exert stronger social attraction, promoting further aggregation and reducing the number of small components, which lowers component-size entropy.

frag_micro_isolate → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward Isolated fish can act as outlying singleton components when local avoidance or escape separates them from neighbors; their centroids then sit farther from the main component centroids, raising the mean distance between component centroids at the meso scale.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_micro_isolate intra_scale A component centroid closer to a shark can intensify local avoidance and detachment of fringe fish, making focal contact isolation more likely.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Components whose centroids are near a shark experience stronger escape pressure; this can cause uneven local splitting or merging across the school, changing how fish counts are distributed among components and thus component-size entropy.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward When some components are much closer to the shark than others, differential escape responses can push their centroids apart or pull them together, altering the mean separation between component centroids.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_macro_component_count upward Many local component-shark encounters can induce localized breakaways and regrouping, which aggregate into changes in the number of connected components across the whole school.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward If components near sharks split off or are stretched away from the main body, the share of fish in the largest component can shrink; thus local threat distance can shape macro fragmentation.
frag_meso_mean_component_size → frag_meso_component_size_entropy intra_scale Larger mean components concentrate fish counts into fewer groups, altering component-size entropy.
frag_meso_mean_component_size → frag_macro_component_count upward For a fixed number of fish, larger mean contact-component size implies that the school is divided into fewer components.

frag_meso_mean_component_size → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward When contact components are larger on average, a smaller number of components can contain a larger share of fish, raising largest-component fraction.

frag_macro_component_count → frag_micro_isolate downward Fragmentation can leave marginal fish outside dense subgroups, making individual contact isolation more likely through changed local neighbor availability.

frag_macro_component_count → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward More contact components change the local grouping context in which fish merge or split, plausibly lowering the average component size observed at the meso level.

frag_macro_component_count → frag_meso_component_size_entropy downward A higher number of components can redistribute fish among subgroups, plausibly raising the entropy of component sizes through repeated splitting and partial re-merging.
frag_macro_component_count → frag_macro_largest_fraction intra_scale A larger number of contact components tends to reduce the share of fish in any single largest component.

frag_macro_largest_fraction → frag_meso_mean_component_size downward When the largest connected fraction grows or shrinks through merging and splitting, the remaining small components are redistributed, so the mean component size can shift dynamically rather than being a fixed identity.

frag_macro_component_count_change → frag_meso_component_size_entropy downward Stepwise splitting or merging of contact components redistributes fish among component sizes, so a macro change in component count can alter the meso entropy of component sizes through the same fragmentation dynamics.

N1 | frag_micro_component_size Contact-component size of focal fish Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: For run r and step t, let G_t=(V_t,E_t) be the undirected graph with fish nodes V_t from agent_states role='fish' and edges E_t from contacts pairs {agent_id,partner_id} at (r,t). For focal fish i in V_t, let C_t(i) be its connected component in G_t. Indicator = |C_t(i)|. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N2 | frag_micro_isolate Focal fish contact isolation flag Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: For fish i at (r,t), let k_i(t)=|{j: (i,j) in E_t or (j,i) in E_t}|. Indicator = 1 if k_i(t)=0, else 0. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N3 | frag_micro_component_shark_distance Focal component centroid to nearest shark distance Scale: micro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Let c_C(t)=mean_{j in C_t(i)} p_j(t) for focal fish i. Let D_i(t)=min_{s in sharks at t} ||c_C(t)-p_s(t)||. Indicator = D_i(t). Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N4 | frag_meso_mean_component_size Mean contact-component size Scale: meso | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Let components of G_t be C_1,...,C_m. Indicator = (1/m) sum_{k=1}^m |C_k|. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N5 | frag_meso_component_size_entropy Contact-component size entropy Scale: meso | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Let p_k=|C_k|/N_t for N_t=sum_j |C_j|. Indicator = -sum_k p_k log2(p_k), with 0 log2 0 treated as 0. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N6 | frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance Mean distance between component centroids Scale: meso | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Let c_k be the position centroid of component C_k. Indicator = (2/(m(m-1))) sum_{a<b} ||c_a-c_b|| for m components; undefined if m<2. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N7 | frag_macro_component_count Number of contact components Scale: macro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Indicator = m, the number of connected components of G_t. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N8 | frag_macro_largest_fraction Largest component fish fraction Scale: macro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Indicator = max_k |C_k| / N_t, where N_t=sum_j |C_j|. Execution: {'2a815b4dfe4f47b8ac2416fac04456e5': {'status': 'not_executed', 'reason': 'explicit_generate_only'}}

N9 | frag_macro_component_count_change Step change in contact-component count Scale: macro | Phenomenon: school_fragmentation Definition: Indicator(t)=m(t)-m(t-1), where m(t) is the number of connected components of G_t.
